title: In vitro transcription of S. pyogenes Cas9 sgRNAs from two complementary oligos
author: Stephen Floor
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.q9gdz3w

steps.title: Design and order oligos
steps.instruction: Order two complementary oligos (~20 nt overlap) that contain the protospacer (capital letters) flanked by a T7 promoter (TAATACGACTCACTATAGG) at the 5' end; replace the final GG of the promoter with the protospacer nucleotides if the target starts with G or GG. Order the constant bottom oligo and the sgRNA forward (GGATCCTAATACGACTCACTATAG) and reverse (AAAAAAGCACCGACTCGG) primers once.

steps.title: Resuspend oligos to 100 µM
steps.instruction: Resuspend each lyophilized oligo in ddH₂O to a final concentration of 100 µM (calculate volume as 10 nmol × 10 = µL ddH₂O).

steps.title: Assemble PCR master mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a 100 µL PCR per sgRNA template (or a master mix for many reactions). Per 100 µL reaction add: 20 µL 5× HF buffer, 2 µL 1 µM top oligo (sgRNA‑specific), 2 µL 1 µM bottom oligo (constant), 2 µL 100 µM sgRNA forward primer, 2 µL 100 µM sgRNA reverse primer, 2 µL dNTPs, 1 µL Phusion polymerase, 69 µL ddH₂O. For many reactions, scale the master mix (e.g., 44 µL 5× HF buffer, 4.4 µL each primer, etc.) and add 5 µL of each sgRNA‑specific top oligo to individual tubes.

steps.title: Perform PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Run the PCR with the following program: 98 °C 2 min; then 30 cycles of 98 °C 30 s, 60 °C 30 s, 72 °C 30 s; finish with 72 °C 1 min and hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Verify PCR product on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Prepare a 2 % agarose gel containing SYBR Safe dye and orange G dye in the loading buffer. Load 5 µL of each PCR reaction plus 5 µL Lonza DNA Marker (50‑1000 bp). Run at ~100 V until the orange G front reaches ~2/3 of the gel length. Image the gel.

steps.title: Purify PCR product
steps.instruction: If a single ~100 nt band is observed, perform a Qiagen PCR cleanup and proceed to transcription. If multiple bands appear, run a preparative 2 % agarose gel (large comb for 200 µL volume), excise the correct band and purify with a Qiagen gel‑extraction kit.

steps.title: Adjust transcription template concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute the purified PCR product to ~100 ng/µL (or adjust volume with DEPC‑treated H₂O) so that each 100 µL transcription reaction contains 10 µL of template (100 ng/µL).

steps.title: Set up in‑vitro transcription
steps.instruction: On ice, assemble the transcription mix in the order listed (keep reagents on ice, but set up at room temperature). For a 100 µL reaction add: 10 µL 10× transcription buffer, 2 µL 1 M DTT (final 20 mM), 20 µL 5 mM A/C/G/U mix (final 5 mM each), 0.5 µL Roche pyrophosphatase (optional, add later when reaction turns cloudy), 10 µL 100 µg/mL T7 polymerase, 10 µL template (100 ng/µL), and 49.5 µL DEPC‑H₂O. Scale proportionally for 1 mL (100 µL each of the above) or 5 mL (500 µL each). Note: cold spermidine in the buffer may precipitate template DNA.

steps.title: Incubate transcription at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the reaction in a water bath or air incubator at 37 °C for 5 hours up to overnight. Do not use a heat block because temperature may exceed 37 °C.

steps.title: Digest DNA template with DNase
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL RNase‑free DNase (RQ1) per 100 µL transcription and continue incubation at 37 °C for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Quench transcription with loading dye
steps.instruction: Add half the reaction volume of 2× denaturing loading dye (e.g., 50 µL to a 100 µL reaction) to stop transcription. The RNA remains stable in this dye overnight, but immediate purification is recommended.

steps.title: Choose RNA cleanup method
steps.instruction: Select either bead‑based cleanup (fast) or gel purification (higher purity).

steps.title: Bead cleanup – bind RNA
steps.instruction: Incubate RNAclean or homemade SPRI beads at room temperature for ~1 hour to equilibrate. Then add 900 µL 100 % ethanol to the transcription, followed by 500 µL SPRI beads. Mix and incubate 5 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Bead cleanup – magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes or until the solution clears. While on the magnet, perform three washes with 1 mL freshly prepared 80 % ethanol (add, wait briefly, then discard). Remove all residual ethanol.

steps.title: Bead cleanup – elute and quantify
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the bead pellet on the magnet for 5‑10 minutes, then remove the tube from the magnet, add 50 µL DEPC‑H₂O, mix, and transfer the supernatant (RNA) to a new tube. Measure RNA concentration using a Qubit fluorometer.

steps.title: Gel purification – prepare denaturing gel
steps.instruction: Cast a 7 M urea, 10 % (29:1) polyacrylamide denaturing gel of sufficient size to accommodate the entire transcription volume.

steps.title: Gel purification – run and visualize
steps.instruction: Run the gel until the xylene bromophenol blue tracking dye reaches the midpoint (a few hours). Image the gel under UV to locate the RNA band just above the xylene front.

steps.title: Gel purification – excise band
steps.instruction: Excise the RNA band with a razor blade and place the slice in an Eppendorf tube (small scale) or a conical tube (large scale).

steps.title: Gel purification – crush gel slice
steps.instruction: Crush the gel slice using a P‑1000 tip (cut off tip) or a glass rod to create small fragments.

steps.title: Gel purification – elute RNA
steps.instruction: Add gel elution buffer enough to cover the fragments (≈500 µL per 100 µL transcription). Rock gently to resuspend.

steps.title: Gel purification – freeze gel bits
steps.instruction: Freeze the suspension for 30 minutes on dry ice or at –80 °C to fracture the gel pieces and improve yield.

steps.title: Gel purification – filter eluate
steps.instruction: For small‑scale reactions, filter the thawed gel bits through a 0.45 µm filter using a cut‑off P‑1000 tip; repeat if SDS precipitates. For large‑scale reactions, vortex the bits, transfer to a flip‑top conical tube filter, and vacuum‑filter until no liquid remains.

steps.title: Gel purification – ethanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Add glycoblue (1 µL per 1 mL) at 1/1000 of the eluate volume and 2.5 volumes of 100 % ethanol. Mix gently.

steps.title: Gel purification – cold incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at –80 °C for at least 1 hour (RNA is stable for months at this temperature).

steps.title: Gel purification – centrifuge pellet
steps.instruction: Spin at 16,000 g for 25 minutes at 4 °C (small scale) or 5,000 g for 25 minutes at 4 °C (large scale). For large scale, resuspend the pellet in 500 µL –20 °C 100 % ethanol, transfer to a microfuge tube, and spin again at 16,000 g for 5 minutes to re‑pellet.

steps.title: Gel purification – wash pellet
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant carefully, then wash the RNA pellet with 500 µL –20 °C 70 % ethanol (add gently, keep tube cold, avoid disturbing the pellet). Remove residual ethanol.

steps.title: Gel purification – final resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed pellet in ~30 µL DEPC‑treated H₂O per 100 µL original transcription volume. Spin at 16,000 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C, then air‑dry the pellet with the cap open for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Quantify final RNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the resuspended RNA to a clean tube and measure its concentration using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer or Qubit fluorometer.
